llm.summary: The skill is a disclosed code-review helper, but one optional reviewer path appears to rely on prompt instructions rather than enforced read-only controls.

dimensions.detail: The skill’s purpose is coherent: it bundles git diffs and asks Codex, Claude, Pi, Droid, Copilot, or OpenCode to review them. Sending code context to external reviewer CLIs and allowing web search are expected for this purpose and are documented.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The activation guidance is broad enough to run after non-trivial code edits, but the runtime contract is review-focused and repeatedly tells reviewers not to modify files or run mutating commands.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The inspected artifact is plain skill documentation plus Python, shell, PowerShell, and test files under .agents/skills/autoreview, with no install hook, startup registration, daemon, cron, or hidden binary payload found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Most engines have concrete read-only or isolation controls, but the Droid path runs droid exec against the repository without an obvious enforced read-only/sandbox flag despite documentation claiming read-only mode. That is a material control gap for an optional external agent engine.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The helper uses temp files and can write user-requested output files; it also reads limited Codex auth configuration values and relies on existing reviewer CLI auth. No unbounded persistence or credential exfiltration behavior was found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable sending review bundles to configured external reviewer CLIs and possibly allowing web search. Prefer the default Codex path or engines with explicit read-only controls; treat the Droid engine as needing manual review or hardening before use on sensitive repositories.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: The broad closeout trigger is real but consistent with an autoreview skill; it is a usability/scope concern rather than evidence of hidden behavior.
[SQP-3] unexpected: The referenced modules/language-detection.md file was not present in the inspected artifact. The main prompt uses senior reviewer framing, but I did not find the specific staff/senior developer persona instructions described by the scanner.
[VirusTotal] expected: VirusTotal telemetry was clean and did not add a negative signal.
